paragraphs.title: The Cancellation of War and the Fortification of Judah

easy.explanation: Rehoboam gathered an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men.
easy.q: How many chosen men did Rehoboam gather to fight against Israel?

easy.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, who delivered it to Rehoboam.
easy.q: Who delivered the word of the LORD to Rehoboam?

answers: He returned from fighting against Jeroboam
easy.explanation: Rehoboam and the people obeyed the LORD and returned from going against Jeroboam.
easy.q: What did Rehoboam do after hearing the word of the LORD?

answers: To bring the kingdom again to himself
medium.explanation: He gathered the army to fight against Israel and bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam.
medium.q: What was Rehoboam’s purpose in gathering the army?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to cities strengthened and prepared for defense.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “cities for defence” mean in this passage?

answers: He destroyed the cities of Judah
He built and fortified cities in Judah
medium.explanation: Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem and built cities for defence in Judah.
medium.q: What did Rehoboam do after the war was cancelled?

answers: The word of the LORD delivered by Shemaiah
challenge.explanation: The LORD commanded them not to fight their brethren, and they obeyed.
challenge.q: What caused Rehoboam and his army to abandon the war?

answers: Captains were appointed and stores of victual, oil, and wine were gathered
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam put captains in the strong holds and stored food, oil, and wine.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the fortification included long-term preparation?

answers: The cities were prepared for military defense
The cities were intended only for commerce
The cities were reserved for priests
challenge.explanation: Shields and spears were weapons, showing that the cities were made strong for defense.
challenge.q: What do the shields and spears placed in every city show?

paragraphs.title: The Priests, Levites, and Seekers of the Lord

easy.explanation: The priests and Levites throughout Israel came to Rehoboam.
easy.q: Who resorted to Rehoboam from all their coasts?

answers: Jeroboam and his sons cast them off from the priest’s office
They wanted to build new cities
easy.explanation: Jeroboam and his sons cast the Levites off from executing the priest’s office unto the LORD.
easy.q: Why did the Levites leave their suburbs and possessions?

easy.explanation: People from all the tribes who sought the LORD came to Jerusalem to sacrifice.
easy.q: Where did those who sought the LORD come?

answers: They came to Judah and Jerusalem
They abandoned the worship of the LORD
medium.explanation: The Levites left their former possessions and came to Judah and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What did the priests and Levites do after leaving the territories of Israel?

medium.explanation: Jeroboam and his sons rejected the Levites and removed them from priestly service.
medium.q: In this context, what does “cast them off” mean?

answers: It caused the fortifications to be removed
It strengthened the kingdom and Rehoboam
medium.explanation: They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam strong.
medium.q: How did the arrival of those seeking the LORD affect Judah?

answers: Jeroboam’s rejection of the priests and Levites led them to Judah and Jerusalem
Jeroboam sent his army to protect Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Because Jeroboam cast them off, the priests and Levites came to Judah and Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage show between Jeroboam’s actions and the strengthening of Jerusalem?

answers: They set their hearts to seek the LORD
They came only to receive food
challenge.explanation: The KJV says they were people who set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel.
challenge.q: What does the passage say about the people who came from all the tribes of Israel?

answers: God’s servants leave Israel, come to Jerusalem, and strengthen Judah
Cities are built, destroyed, and returned to Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the departure of the Levites, the arrival of seekers in Jerusalem, and the strengthening of Judah.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events in verses 13–17?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam took Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth, to wife.
easy.q: Whom did Rehoboam take to wife?

easy.explanation: The passage says Rehoboam loved Maachah above all his wives and concubines.
easy.q: Whom did Rehoboam love above all his wives and concubines?

easy.explanation: The passage states that Rehoboam begat twenty and eight sons.
easy.q: How many sons did Rehoboam beget?

answers: Twenty and eight wives and threescore concubines
medium.explanation: The KJV says he took eighteen wives and threescore concubines.
medium.q: How many wives and concubines did Rehoboam have?

answers: Women in a secondary marital position
medium.explanation: The passage distinguishes concubines from the king’s wives as part of his household.
medium.q: What does “concubines” refer to in this passage?

medium.explanation: They bore him twenty and eight sons and threescore daughters.
medium.q: What did Rehoboam’s wives and concubines bear him?

answers: Rehoboam loved her above all his wives and concubines
She was the mother of every son
challenge.explanation: The text specifically says that Rehoboam loved Maachah above all the others.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes Maachah’s favored position?

answers: They show that he had a large royal household
They show that he had very few children
They show that all his children were priests
challenge.explanation: The many names and large numbers present Rehoboam’s extensive royal family.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the names and numbers of Rehoboam’s children?

answers: His marriages are described, followed by the children born to him
His descendants are described before his marriages
The passage connects the two in no way
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from describing his wives to describing the sons and daughters they bore.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Rehoboam’s marriages and his descendants in these verses?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief.
easy.q: Whom did Rehoboam make the chief?

easy.explanation: Abijah was made ruler among his brethren.
easy.q: What position did Rehoboam give Abijah?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam gave his children victual in abundance.
easy.q: What did Rehoboam give his children in the fenced cities?

answers: Because he thought to make him king
To have him build the temple
medium.explanation: The passage says Rehoboam made Abijah chief because he thought to make him king.
medium.q: Why did Rehoboam make Abijah the chief?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Rehoboam acted with wisdom in arranging his children throughout the land.
medium.q: What does the phrase “he dealt wisely” indicate about Rehoboam’s actions?

answers: He gave them cities and abundant food
He appointed all of them as priests
medium.explanation: He dispersed them throughout the fenced cities and gave them victual in abundance.
medium.q: How did Rehoboam provide for his children?

answers: He intended Abijah to become king
He intended to abolish the monarchy
He intended to give Judah to Jeroboam
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam made Abijah chief because he thought to make him king.
challenge.q: What does Abijah’s appointment reveal about Rehoboam’s intention for the future?

answers: He was placed in a position of authority among the royal family spread through those cities
He left all the cities of Judah
challenge.explanation: Abijah was made chief while Rehoboam wisely distributed his children throughout the fenced cities.
challenge.q: How was Abijah connected with the fortified cities?

answers: They received abundant food, and Rehoboam desired many wives for them
They received no support from their father
challenge.explanation: The final verse says Rehoboam gave them victual in abundance and desired many wives.
challenge.q: Which detail is surprising about Rehoboam’s children?
